cases.question: What recalls are there for a 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
NHTSA lists 6 recalls for the 2017 Honda Civic. Some of them cover only certain body styles, so I've noted that for each one:

All body styles (sedan, coupe and hatchback):
- 18V663000: Steering. A loose magnet in the power steering sensor can make the steering assist push the wrong way during a full-lock turn. Dealers replace the steering gearbox.
- 23V858000: Fuel pump. The pump can fail and stall the engine while you're driving. Dealers replace the fuel pump module.
- 26V332000: Air bags. The front passenger seat weight sensor can crack and short out. Dealers replace the sensor.

Sedan and coupe only:
- 17V706000: The right halfshaft may be weak and can break, which can let the car roll away if the parking brake isn't set. Dealers inspect it and replace it if needed.

Hatchback and Type R only:
- 18V817000: The owner's guide may be missing or missing child-seat anchor information. Dealers replace the owner's information kit.
- 18V266000: Seatback pads sold as replacement parts may block the side air bags. Dealers replace the pads.

None of these is marked "park it" or "park outside." Every repair is free at a Honda dealer. You can also call Honda at 1-888-234-2138.

Each recall covers only certain cars, so check yours by entering its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you share the VIN or tell me the body style, I can tell you which of these apply.

cases.question: Is there a power steering recall on the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Yes. NHTSA lists a power steering recall for the 2017 Honda Civic: 18V663000 (electric power steering).

What's wrong: a magnet in the steering torque sensor might not be held in place properly. If it comes loose, turning the wheel all the way can push the steering assist the wrong way. That makes the car harder to control and raises the risk of a crash.

The fix: Honda dealers replace the steering gearbox for free. Honda calls this recall C2N / P2O, and you can reach Honda at 1-888-234-2138.

This recall covers only certain 2017 Civics, not every one. To see whether yours is included and still needs the fix, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you send me the VIN, I can also check your exact version and look for other open recalls on it.

cases.question: Is there a fuel pump recall for the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Yes. NHTSA lists a fuel pump recall for the 2017 Honda Civic: 23V858000.

- The problem: the fuel pump inside the tank can fail. If it does, the engine can stall while you're driving, which raises the risk of a crash.
- Which cars: it covers certain Civic sedans, coupes, hatchbacks and Type Rs from 2013 to 2023. "Certain" means not every one of those cars is included. It expands earlier recalls 20V-314 and 21V-215.
- The fix: Honda dealers replace the fuel pump module for free. Honda's recall codes are KGC and KGD, and owner letters went out September 6, 2024.

To see if your car is included, enter its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or call Honda at 1-888-234-2138. If you send me the VIN, I can also check the other 2017 Civic recalls that might apply to your car.

cases.question: Is there a recall for the halfshaft or driveshaft on a 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Yes. NHTSA recall 17V706000 covers the right front halfshaft (driveshaft) on certain 2017 Honda Civic Sedan and Coupe models. It does not include the Hatchback or Type R.

What's wrong: The right halfshaft may not have been heat-treated correctly, which makes it weaker. It can break, and then the engine can't move the car. If the parking brake isn't set, the car could also roll away.

The fix: Honda dealers check the halfshaft's serial number, replace it if needed and align the front wheels, all free. Honda's number for this recall is K0E, and Honda customer service is 1-888-234-2138.

Whether your car is included depends on its body style and VIN. To check your exact car, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. You can also send me your VIN and I'll decode it to confirm the body style. That would also let me check the other 2017 Civic recalls for you.

cases.question: Was there ever a recall about the owner's manual for the 2017 Civic?

answer.text:
Yes. NHTSA recall 18V817000 covers some 2017-2018 Honda Civic Hatchback and Civic Type R cars. The owner's guide may have been left out of the car, or it may be missing required information about the child seat anchors. That information is required under safety standard FMVSS 225. Dealers will replace the owner's information kit for free. Honda's code for this recall is O3A, and Honda customer service is at 1-888-234-2138.

This recall covers only the Hatchback and Type R, so a 2017 Civic Sedan or Coupe isn't included. If you tell me your body style or VIN, I can check whether it matches. For the official status of your car, enter the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

cases.question: Which air bag recalls are listed for the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
NHTSA lists 2 air bag recalls for the 2017 Honda Civic:

1. 18V266000: Air bags. This covers certain 2017 Civic Hatchback and Civic Type R cars. Replacement front seatback pads were made without the openings that let the seat-mounted side air bags come out. In a crash, the side air bags might not deploy correctly. Fix: dealers replace the front seatback pads for free.

2. 26V332000: Front passenger seat weight sensor. This is a broad recall. For 2017 cars it lists the Civic (sedan), Civic hatchback, Civic coupe and Civic Type R. The sensor can crack and short circuit, and the air bags may then deploy when they shouldn't during a crash. Fix: dealers replace the sensor for free. Owner letters went out July 7, 2026.

Not every recall covers every 2017 Civic, because body styles differ. To see if either one applies to your car, send me your VIN, or check nhtsa.gov/recalls for the official status of your specific car.

cases.question: What recalls does a 2006 Ford Ranger have?

answer.text:
⚠️ DO NOT DRIVE WARNING: NHTSA marks four 2006 Ranger air bag recalls "park it": 18V022000, 18V023000, 17V787000 and 17V788000. Ford asks owners of affected trucks not to drive them until they're repaired, because the front air bag inflators can explode in a crash and throw metal fragments.

NHTSA lists 12 recalls for the 2006 Ford Ranger. Each one only covers some trucks, depending on things like build date or replacement parts, so this list doesn't show which ones apply to your truck:

Air bags (Takata inflators):
- 18V022000 (passenger) and 18V023000 (driver): park it. About 33,310 2006 Rangers.
- 17V787000 (driver) and 17V788000 (passenger): park it. These are the final fix that replaces the earlier temporary repairs. Trucks fixed under the earlier recalls need to go back to the dealer.
- 16V036000 (driver) and 15V322000 (passenger): earlier temporary repairs, now replaced by the two above.
- 21V076000 and 21V081000: replacement inflators installed as service parts that may explode.
- 23V125000 and 23V306000: replacement passenger inflators that may have been installed wrong. 23V306000 replaces 23V125000.

Other:
- 11V352000: replacement multi-function switch parts. The switch can fail and stop the turn signals, tail lights, hazards or brake lights from working.
- 05V520000: wiper motor built without grease, so the wipers can stop working.

All repairs are free. To see which recalls are open on your truck, enter its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, or call Ford at 1-866-436-7332. If an air bag recall is open, please don't drive the truck. Ask Ford about having it towed to the dealer.

cases.question: Are there any recalls on a 2006 Ford Ranger?

answer.text:
⚠️ DO NOT DRIVE WARNING: NHTSA has "park it" (do not drive) recalls for some 2006 Ford Rangers: 18V022000 (passenger air bag) and 18V023000 (driver air bag), plus 17V787000 (driver) and 17V788000 (passenger). In a crash, the air bag inflator in affected trucks can explode and throw metal pieces at the people inside. If your truck is affected and hasn't been fixed, don't drive it. Call Ford at 1-866-436-7332 or a Ford dealer. The repair is free.

NHTSA lists 12 recalls for the 2006 Ranger. Each one covers only some trucks, depending on when and where they were built:

Air bags (the most serious ones):
- 18V022000 and 18V023000: Do not drive. The passenger and driver inflators can explode.
- 17V787000 and 17V788000: Do not drive. These are the final fixes for the driver and passenger inflators. They replace the temporary fixes in 16V036000 and 15V322000. If your truck got the temporary fix, it still needs to go back to a dealer.
- 16V036000 and 15V322000: Earlier inflator recalls.
- 21V076000 and 21V081000: Replacement inflators installed as service parts may explode.
- 23V306000 (replaces 23V125000): Replacement passenger inflators may have been installed wrong.

Other:
- 11V352000: A faulty multi-function switch can stop the turn signals, tail lights, hazard lights or brake lights from working.
- 05V520000: The wiper motor may be missing grease, so the wipers can stop working.

To see which recalls are still open on your truck, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you send me the VIN, I can also decode it and give you more detail.

cases.question: The tail lights on my 2006 Ford Ranger keep flickering. Is there a recall for that?

answer.text:
SAFETY WARNING FIRST: NHTSA lists four "do not drive" air bag recalls for certain 2006 Ford Rangers: 18V022000, 18V023000, 17V787000 and 17V788000. The front air bag inflators can explode in a crash and throw metal fragments. Please enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls right away. If any of these show as open, don't drive the truck. Call Ford at 1-866-436-7332 to have it repaired for free, often with towing or a mobile repair.

About your tail lights: there's one related recall, 11V352000. It covers a faulty multi-function (turn signal) switch that can stop the tail, brake, turn and hazard lights from working. For a 2006 Ranger, though, it only covers replacement switches sent to dealers as service parts, not the switch the truck was built with. It would only apply if your switch was replaced at some point. A VIN check at nhtsa.gov/recalls or a call to a Ford dealer will tell you.

If that recall doesn't apply, flickering tail lights often come from:
- a bad ground or corroded connection at the tail light sockets or the trailer wiring
- loose or worn bulbs or sockets
- a failing multi-function switch
- damaged wiring where the harness runs along the frame

I'm not a mechanic, so please have it inspected, especially since your brake lights may be affected. I tried to pull owners' complaints for this truck, but that data isn't available right now.

Other recalls for 2006 Rangers include more air bag campaigns. Your VIN check will show everything that's open on your truck.

cases.question: What are owners complaining about with the brakes on the 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
Owners have filed 607 complaints with NHTSA about the 2017 Honda Civic. 39 of them involve the brakes, and 38 are listed under "Service Brakes." That's a small share. The most common complaint area is steering, with 174 reports.

The newest brake complaints describe:
- Electric parking brake problems: One owner says it engaged by itself after the car was turned off and showed an "Electric Parking Brake Problem" warning.
- Brake system failure warnings: One owner says the car wouldn't start, the brake pedal locked up and a brake system warning came on.
- Several warning lights at once: One owner saw the ABS, power steering and check-engine lights come on together, with no driving problem.
- Noise: Owners report squealing when stopping and a loud screeching from the rear that stopped when they pressed the brake pedal.

None of the recent brake complaints mention a crash, fire or injury. These are reports owners send to NHTSA, and NHTSA doesn't verify them. They aren't recalls and don't prove there's a defect.

If your Civic has any of these signs, especially a brake warning light or a pedal that feels wrong, please have the brakes checked by a mechanic soon. I can also look up recalls for the 2017 Civic, or brake parts if you tell me your VIN or whether it's a sedan, coupe or hatchback.

cases.question: Does recall 17V706000 apply to my 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
It depends on your Civic's body style. NHTSA lists recall 17V706000 for some 2017 Civic Sedans and Coupes only. The right front halfshaft (the axle) may not have been heat-treated properly, so it can break. If it breaks, the engine can't move the car, and the car could roll away if the parking brake isn't on. Honda's fix is free: the dealer checks the halfshaft's serial number, replaces the part if needed and aligns the front wheels. Honda's code for this recall is K0E.

- If your car is a Sedan or Coupe, it may be covered.
- If it's a Hatchback or a Type R, this recall doesn't cover it.

Even a Sedan or Coupe may not be covered, because the recall only includes "certain" cars. To check your exact car, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. You can also send me the 17-character VIN or tell me the body style, and I'll go through all the recalls listed for a 2017 Civic.

cases.question: Which recalls apply to my 2017 Honda Civic?

answer.text:
NHTSA lists 6 recalls for the 2017 Honda Civic. Some cover only certain body styles, so which ones apply to your car depends on whether it's a sedan, coupe, hatchback or Type R.

These cover all 2017 Civic body styles:
- 18V663000: The steering assist could push the wrong way during a full-lock turn. The dealer replaces the steering gearbox.
- 23V858000: The fuel pump could fail, and the engine could stall. The dealer replaces the fuel pump module.
- 26V332000: The front passenger seat weight sensor could crack, and the air bags could deploy when they shouldn't in a crash. The dealer replaces the sensor.

These depend on your body style:
- 17V706000 (sedan and coupe only): The right halfshaft could break. The car could then roll away if the parking brake isn't set.
- 18V266000 (hatchback and Type R only): Replacement seatback pads could block the side air bags.
- 18V817000 (hatchback and Type R only): The owner's guide may be missing or incomplete.

None of these are marked "park it" or "park outside." Even so, a recall only covers some cars in each model year. To check your car's official status, enter its VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. If you send me the VIN or tell me the body style, I can narrow this list. All of these repairs are free at a Honda dealer.

cases.question: Does the air bag recall 18V266000 cover my 2017 Civic?

answer.text:
It depends on your Civic's body style.

**18V266000** only covers certain **2017 Civic Hatchbacks and Civic Type Rs**. On those cars, replacement front seatback pads were made without the openings the seat-mounted side air bags need, so the air bags might not deploy properly. The fix is free: dealers replace the seatback pads. If you have a 2017 Civic sedan or coupe, this recall doesn't apply to your car.

There's also another air bag recall, **26V332000**, which covers 2017 Civic sedans, coupes, hatchbacks and Type Rs. The front passenger seat weight sensor may crack, which can make the air bags deploy the wrong way in a crash. Dealers replace the sensor for free.

Neither recall says you need to stop driving or park outside.

Which body style is your Civic? You can also send me the 17-character VIN and I'll decode it. To see the official open recalls for your specific car, enter your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.
